About

A technician's instinct, applied to data.

I'm Bosco, a technology enthusiast and data analyst based in Kigali, Rwanda.

I've always been curious about how things work. From electrical systems and electronics to software, connected devices and data, I've found myself drawn to the thinking behind technology: how things are built, how they communicate, and how they can be made better.

I enjoy exploring problems, understanding how systems work, working with information and finding practical ways to use technology to make things more efficient.

My interests span data analytics, engineering, IoT, automation, software development and emerging technologies. I'm particularly drawn to the possibilities that emerge when these fields come together to solve real-world problems.

I'm naturally curious, always exploring new ideas, experimenting with different tools and looking for opportunities to turn concepts into practical solutions.

For me, technology is more than a profession. It's a continuous process of curiosity, learning, building and discovering what's possible.

What I've actually built

01
Solar Engineering · Closed-Loop Control · Arduino UNO

Solar System Tracker (Dual-Axis Arduino Sun Tracker)

An Arduino-based closed-loop system that tilts a solar panel to follow the sun through the day for maximum irradiance capture.

The Problem

A fixed solar panel only faces the sun directly for a short window around midday — during morning and late afternoon hours, cosine losses significantly reduce power output.

The Context

A hands-on hardware engineering project exploring how an embedded microcontroller and low-cost optical sensors can automatically orient a PV array along two axes.

The Approach

Compare light readings from four LDR sensors positioned in a quadrant divider around the panel, then drive azimuth and elevation servo motors toward whichever quadrant reads brighter until all sensors balance within a deadband threshold.

Arduino Uno4x LDR sensorsDual Servo motorsSolar PV panelClosed-loop calibration

The Result

The panel tracked the sun's movement smoothly across the sky, maintaining perpendicular alignment and delivering up to 30–35% higher daily energy yield compared to a fixed horizontal panel.

The Lesson

Simple analog sensors can achieve reliable closed-loop control when paired with proper deadband hysteresis so servos settle cleanly without hunting.

02
Embedded Systems · GSM Telemetry · ULK Final Project

Arduino Laser-Based Security System with GSM Alert

Final-year electrical engineering project — an invisible laser tripwire and PIR perimeter alarm that dispatches instant SMS alerts over cellular GSM.

The Problem

Design an affordable, standalone intrusion-detection system for a doorway or perimeter that alerts property owners remotely without relying on Wi-Fi or grid electricity.

The Context

Final-year capstone project for my Advanced Diploma (A1) in Electrical Technology at Université Libre de Kigali (ULK) — defended December 2025.

The Approach

Combine a focused laser beam aimed at an LDR voltage-divider with PIR motion sensing. When an intruder breaks the beam, an Arduino UNO R3 triggers local acoustic/strobe alarms and commands a SIM800L GSM module to send an immediate SMS alert.

Arduino UNO R3SIM800L GSMLaser DiodeLDR SensorPIR HC-SR5014x4 KeypadTP4056 + 18650 Li-IonLM2596 Buck Converter

The Result

A battle-tested hardware prototype capable of instant sub-second beam-break detection and reliable cellular SMS dispatch during power outages using its regulated dual-18650 battery pack.

The Lesson

Cellular GSM modules draw 2A current spikes during transmission bursts — regulating the 4.1V power rail with a buck converter and bypass capacitors was essential to prevent microcontroller brownouts.

03
Computer Vision · Biometric Access Control · Python & OpenCV

Security Face Recognition System

An automated biometric security and access-control system using Python and OpenCV to detect faces, match facial encodings, and control door lock relays.

The Problem

Physical keys and PIN codes can be lost, shared, or shoulder-surfed. Restricted labs and entry points need contactless biometric verification that logs every access attempt automatically.

The Context

A computer-vision security project combining my Applied Machine Learning in Python training with hardware relay actuation for smart doorway access control.

The Approach

Capture live video frames, detect facial landmarks, extract 128-dimensional facial embeddings, and compute Euclidean distance against authorized profiles. Verified matches trigger a serial signal to unlock the solenoid relay; unknown faces trigger a security alert and timestamped snapshot log.

IDENTITY MATCH: Niyonkuru Jean Paul (Confidence: 98.7%)

[ACCESS GRANTED] Timestamp logged to SQLite audit table.
PythonOpenCVface_recognition (dlib)128-D Facial EmbeddingsSerial / Relay ControlAccess Audit Logging

The Result

A responsive real-time recognition pipeline that accurately distinguishes registered personnel from unauthorized visitors under varying indoor lighting and actuates physical lock hardware in under 350ms.

The Lesson

Lighting normalization (CLAHE histogram equalization) before computing facial embeddings dramatically reduces false rejections when ambient room light shifts.
